prompt: Coupon stores a code and a percent; the fields and constructor are done. Implement equals (getClass-based, null-safe on both fields), hashCode with Objects.hash, and toString formatted like "SAVE10 (10%)" so Coupons behave correctly in a HashSet.
explanation: The equals contract requires reflexivity, symmetry, and null-safety, and the getClass() comparison guarantees symmetry even against subclasses (an anonymous subclass in the tests would break an instanceof-based version one-sidedly). Objects.equals handles a null code without a NullPointerException, and Objects.hash combines the fields so that equal objects always produce equal hash codes -- the property HashSet depends on to detect duplicates. Without a matching hashCode, the set would file equal coupons in different buckets and keep both.
hints: Standard equals skeleton: if (this == o) return true; if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false; then cast and compare fields.
Compare the String field with Objects.equals(code, other.code) so null codes cannot throw.
hashCode is one line -- return Objects.hash(code, percent); -- and toString is code + " (" + percent + "%)";
